title: Waterloo region municipalities launch a new pilot program, inviting developers to collaborate on building for the future
content: Waterloo - As of November 5, 2026, developers and builders across Waterloo region are invited to participate in a new voluntary pilot program to explore ways to make their developments more energy-efficient, resilient, and sustainable.

Through WR Community Energy , Waterloo Region municipalities are working together to advance a harmonized approach to building for our changing environment. The High-Performance Development Standards (HPDS) Pilot Program is the next step in exploring how high-performance development practices can be applied to real-world projects.

The HPDS are a suggested set of standards for consideration in new development applications in the Cities of Cambridge, Kitchener, and Waterloo, and the Townships of North Dumfries, Wellesley, Wilmot, and Woolwich.

Through standard planning application processes, this Pilot Program gives developers an opportunity to put these practices into action, share what works, and help shape future approaches to development in Waterloo region. These practices can help reduce energy and water use and keep utility bills low, prepare buildings and communities for a changing climate, and make better use of resources.

The program was developed through extensive engagement with municipal staff, the development industry and the community, technical analysis, and a review of best practices. It is the next step in exploring how these practices can work in real-world projects.
The pilot will explore measures such as:

Participation in the Pilot Program is voluntary and open to interested developers and builders through the planning application process. Participants will be invited to submit a Statement of Interest, with projects selected that will ensure a mix of building types and locations across Waterloo region.
All participating projects will be recognized with additional Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Energy Innovator recognition awarded to builders and developers based on the number of HPDS targets achieved.
This is an opportunity for developers and builders to showcase leadership in high-performance development, share lessons from real-world projects, and help shape future development in the Region.
The Pilot Program creates a space to explore what works, recognize industry leadership, and advance more efficient, resilient, and sustainable communities.
Interested in participating?
Visit the HPDS project page to learn more about the standards.

title: Statement from Mayor Berry Vrbanovic on the 2026 Federal Budget: Masters of Our Destiny
content: Today’s federal budget recognizes the real pressures people are feeling across Canada and here in Kitchener. We see them in the cost of groceries and housing, in our workplaces and across our neighbourhoods. This moment calls for meaningful action.

We welcome the federal government’s focus on making life more affordable and building a stronger, more independent Canadian economy. The budget identifies Canada’s highly skilled workforce, research institutions and capacity for innovation as strengths that can help our country compete and prosper.

Kitchener is ready to contribute. At the heart of Canada’s innovation and technology corridor, our community brings together skilled workers, entrepreneurs, researchers and companies developing ideas and products for markets at home and around the world. Kitchener has an important role to play as Canada strengthens its economic independence, helps Canadian businesses scale and creates good jobs here at home.

Housing is central to a more affordable future. Today’s budget reflects a shared commitment to accelerating homebuilding and lowering costs, to make housing more accessible to everyone in our community.

Kitchener is ready to be a strong partner and we have a proven record of delivering. We have modernized approvals, invested municipal funding, made land available and supported housing providers. Together, these efforts have helped enable roughly 2,000 affordable homes across 40 projects, including more than 184 supportive homes, with more underway.

New federal support for municipal e-permitting and technology-enabled approvals is also encouraging. Kitchener’s experience shows that modern processes and responsible stewardship can deliver meaningful results and we are ready to share what we have learned.

We also applaud the federal government’s 10-year $29-billion commitment towards supportive housing and services for people and communities, which was also announced in today’s budget. We recognize the difference an investment of this scale can make and will require orders of governments and communities to work together to get it right.

We’re pleased to see new investment through the Build Communities Strong Fund. Here in Kitchener, this partnership is helping us grow with purpose and create welcoming places where residents can connect, stay active and take part in community life.

The new $1.5-billion investment in arenas and community recreation facilities is a welcome opportunity for growing communities like ours. Recreation is a core municipal service and an important part of a healthy, connected city. Arenas, pools, sports fields and community centres are where children learn new skills, neighbours get to know one another, older adults stay active and people of all ages and abilities find a sense of belonging.

Kitchener’s soon-to-open Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park reflects that approach. Supported through the Build Communities Strong Fund, it will be a welcoming hub where people can be active, spend time together and participate in community life.

As Kitchener grows, we will continue to advocate for sustained investment in the infrastructure, facilities and services residents depend on. These investments help us build complete neighbourhoods, support more housing and provide stability for the future.

Kitchener is ready to work with the Government of Canada to turn national priorities into local results. We will bring our experience in housing delivery, our culture of innovation and our strong community partnerships to that work, while keeping the focus on what matters to people here at home.

title: Carbon Monoxide Awareness Week is a reminder to test alarms and protect your household
content: A quick test today could save a life tomorrow. During Carbon Monoxide Awareness Week from November 1 to 7, Kitchener Fire is reminding residents that carbon monoxide alarms are not only essential for home safety, they're required by law in homes with fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces or attached garages. Carbon monoxide is a dangerous gas that cannot be seen, smelled or tasted, making a working alarm the only reliable way to detect its presence in your home.
This week, take a few minutes to test your carbon monoxide alarms and follow these tips to help keep your household safe:

Working carbon monoxide and smoke alarms save lives. They provide an early warning when every second counts, giving you and your loved ones the time needed to respond safely. Taking a few minutes to test your alarms today can help protect the people who matter most and provide peace of mind throughout the year.
Learn more at KitchenerFire.ca

title: Kitchener launches Christkindl Entertainment Series with 10 days of live entertainment celebrating 30 years of holiday magic
content: Kitchener, ON – As Christkindl Market celebrates its 30th anniversary this December with an expanded festival schedule, the community is invited to experience the new Christkindl Entertainment Series - 10 exciting days of live music, family experiences, holiday traditions and festive entertainment from December 3 to 13.

What started as a volunteer-run holiday celebration has become one of the region's busiest, most cherished events, bringing more than 100,000 visitors annually from across the province. As the festival has grown, it has expanded from the smaller Christmas market first held in 1997 to a 10-day celebration of the season in 2026 with free activities, live entertainment and winter magic for all ages.

This year, the new Christkindl Entertainment Series will pair nightly headline performances and special events with a full schedule of appearances by local musicians, choirs, cultural organizations, dance groups and community performers, showcasing the talent and traditions that make Waterloo Region unique.
The anniversary lineup combines the community favourites visitors have come to know and love over three decades with new events introducing even more ways to celebrate the magic of the season.

"For 30 years, Christkindl has brought people together through the traditions, experiences and local talent that make the holiday season special in Kitchener," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "The new Christkindl Entertainment Series shines a spotlight on the musicians, performers and artists who help create the magic of Christkindl each year. With a full 10-day lineup of free entertainment, and now with the addition of new ticketed experiences, we're giving residents and visitors even more ways to celebrate the season and create holiday memories with family and friends while supporting our local arts community."

The Christkindl Entertainment Series begins December 3 with the 30th Anniversary Opening Ceremonies at Carl Zehr Square and continues with 10 days of live music, family experiences and holiday entertainment. Alongside a full schedule of free programming, including The Golden Keys, Holiday Jukebox featuring Pulse X, the Christkindl Holiday Hoedown, Great Canadian Dueling Pianos and Jersey Nights, the series will introduce new ticketed experiences such as the Royal Pancake Breakfast, Jingle Bell Brunch, Epic Eagles: A Very Merry Take It Easy Christmas, Signal Hill's East Coast Christmas Kitchen Party and the Disco All the Way party.

"The Christkindl Entertainment Series allows us to honour the traditions that have made Christkindl special for 30 years while creating new experiences for audiences of all ages," said Steve Roth, Manager of Special Events for the City of Kitchener. "Whether you're attending a free concert in the Musik Haus tent, taking part in a family brunch or coming together with family, friends and colleagues to see one of our fantastic headliners, there are more opportunities than ever to be part of the Christkindl experience."

title: Learn Essential First Aid and CPR skills
content: Whether you're starting a new job, preparing for a volunteer role, completing a school placement or simply want to be ready when an emergency happens, the City of Kitchener offers First Aid & CPR Training to help residents build confidence and lifesaving skills.

The City offers WSIB-approved First Aid, CPR-C and AED training that is recognized by employers across Ontario. Participants receive certification valid for three years and gain practical, hands-on experience responding to workplace, home and community emergencies.
Courses are available on weekdays and weekends, making it easy to fit training into your schedule. Training options include:
Whether you're learning lifesaving skills for the first time or renewing your certification, there's a course to meet your needs.
These courses are ideal for employees, job seekers, post-secondary students, volunteers, caregivers, and anyone who wants to be prepared to help when it matters most.
Ready to get certified? Register online, at your local community centre, pool or the Service Kitchener counter at City Hall and take the first step toward becoming emergency ready.

title: Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park to feature Canada's first multi-sport glass floor
content: Innovative technology will expand recreation opportunities, improve accessibility, and attract tournaments and events to Kitchener

Kitchener, ON – Residents visiting the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park will soon have access to a recreation experience unlike any other in Canada. Available for use starting in early 2027, the Centre’s new quad gymnasium will feature Canada's first multi-sport glass floor, making it home to one of the largest installations of its kind in the world.

The innovative multi-sport surface w ill provide more opportunities for recreation, sport, tournaments and community events while giving residents access to the same playing surface used for decades at sport venues and international competitions globally.

"Great community spaces should evolve alongside the people who use them," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "The multi-sport glass floor reflects the kind of future we're building in Kitchener, one that embraces innovation while creating more diverse opportunities for residents to compete, connect and belong close to home. This floor gives the community access to a unique recreation experience typically found at premier sport venues and, as the first installation of its kind in Canada, will help create better recreational and competitive sport experiences while also attracting new events and visitors that support local businesses and strengthen Kitchener's economy."
The multi-sport glass floor will support a wide variety of sports including pickleball, basketball, volleyball, floor hockey, futsal, badminton, wheelchair basketball and wheelchair pickleball.

Starting November 14, when the Cowan Recreation Centre officially opens, visitors will have a unique opportunity to get a behind-the-scenes look at the technology that will be located beneath the multi-sport glass panels. Installation of the floor is expected to be complete early in the new year.

While this flooring system, designed and installed by ASB GlassFloor, is the first of its kind in C anada, it is used in the United States and across Europe, including venues in Germany, Greece, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

The flooring system uses LED lighting located under glass floor panels to display digital sport lines directly onto the playing surface. Unlike traditional gymnasium floors that rely on multiple p ermanently painted or taped lines, the sport lines on this floor can be quickly and easily reconfigured at the touch of a button depending on which sport is being played. Only the lines required for the sport being played are displayed at any time, reducing visual clutter and creating a cleaner environment that can be easier for participants to navigate. Importantly, flexible sport configurations also mean more support for accessible and inclusive play – transitioning from wheelchair basketball to wheelchair pickleball and back to traditional volleyball is easy and safe.

With a surface that exceeds internationally recognized standards for shock absorption and slip resistance, combined with a durable, high-performance surface that supports wheelchair sports and adaptive recreation programming, the technology helps create a more inclusive recreation experience for residents of all abilities. The floor is certified by the International Basketball Federation (FIBA), International Volleyball Federation (FIVB), and International Handball Federation (IHF).

Beyond enhancing the user experience, the floor was selected for its long-term value. The multi-sport glass floor does not require refinishing or resurfacing on a regular basis and can accommodate a broader range of activities without protective floor coverings. Less downtime and fewer seasonal maintenance closers mean lower maintenance costs and more programming time for residents.

By combining digital flexibility, enhanced accessibility and reduced maintenance requirements, the glass sports floor creates new possibilities for how the space can be programmed and used while delivering long-term value for residents and the community.
Quick facts
First glass sports floor installation in Canada
One of the largest installations in the world
Can be reconfigured at the touch of a button to support a wide range of sports
Only the lines required for the activity being played are displayed
Supports wheelchair sports and adaptive recreation programming
No sanding, resurfacing or seasonal shutdowns required
About the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park
The Cowan Recreation Centre is among the largest and most sustainable municipally owned recreation centres in Canada.

The Centre offers diverse recreation opportunities with a quad gymnasium, FIFA-sized indoor turf field, cricket practice nets, competition and leisure pools, and an indoor walking track, supporting sports and activities ranging from basketball and soccer to pickleball, badminton and swimming.

The facility is the most accessible building ever constructed by the City of Kitchener, designed to meet the City's highest accessibility standards and shaped through input from residents with lived experience. It features pool ramps, wider pathways, tactile wayfinding elements and accessible viewing areas.
Built to host provincial and national competitions, tournaments and major events, the Centre will help showcase Kitchener, support local businesses and generate economic benefits for the community.

title: Statement from Mayor Vrbanovic on Ontario’s 2026 Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review
content: Today’s provincial economic update comes at a time when many Kitchener businesses and workers are dealing with real uncertainty caused by U.S. tariffs and changing global trade conditions.

Ontario’s 2026 Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review includes measures aimed at supporting workers and businesses, including the recently announced $8.7-billion Canada-Ontario action plan for tariff-affected sectors, expanded access to provincial trade and financing programs, and employment and training supports for workers affected by layoffs.

Here in the City of Kitchener, we know that ours is one of Canada’s most trade-exposed regions, and 15 per cent of our workforce is employed in manufacturing. Behind those numbers are local families, small businesses, manufacturers and employers who contribute every day to the strength of our community.

That’s why we welcome the province’s continued focus on helping workers and businesses respond to tariff pressures. These supports can help local employers manage uncertainty, pursue new opportunities and, most importantly, keep people working.

We’re doing our part as well. Through our Tariff and Trade Task Force and Plan to Support Local and Protect Jobs , we’re bringing local partners together, using City spending to support Canadian and local businesses, and helping Kitchener companies adapt and reach new markets. Measures that reduce the cost of investment and research can also help our manufacturing and innovation sectors continue to invest and create jobs here at home.

Municipalities have an essential role in Ontario’s economic future. The roads, transit, water systems and other infrastructure we build and maintain help create jobs and make new housing and private investment possible. As Kitchener continues to grow, we need strong, predictable and long-term provincial investment in municipal infrastructure so we can keep pace with that growth.

We’re also pleased to see continued progress on the new Highway 7 between Kitchener and Guelph, including the replacement of the Frederick Street bridge, as well as recent improvements along the Kitchener GO Line. Better connections give people more options to get to work and help connect Kitchener businesses to opportunities across Ontario.

We’ll continue working with the Province of Ontario and our partners to make sure Kitchener workers and businesses can access the supports they need, while continuing to advocate for the infrastructure a growing Kitchener and Waterloo Region need for the future.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener Media@kitchener.ca

title: Kitchener Fire Department: Major incident report – October 27, 2026
content: At 5:30 a.m. this morning, Kitchener Fire crews responded to reports of a residential structure fire on Weber St E.
All occupants safely self-evacuated. Fire spread was contained to contents only.  Residents of the main floor apartment will be displaced and are being supported.
There are no reported civilian or firefighter injuries at this time.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Kitchener Fire is working closely with Waterloo Regional Police Service.
